caption: The drawing shows a color plan view of a garden and surrounding area divided into several distinct sections by paths and fences. In the upper section, there is a circular, segmented garden with triangular flowerbeds filled with various brightly colored flowers (red, yellow, pink, white) and plants, bordered by brown paths converging at a central point. Adjacent to these beds on the right, there are rectangular plots arranged in a grid, containing crops or vegetables in green and tan hues. Below the flowerbeds, a pathway curves around a cluster of trees and a rectangular structure with a purple roof and adjacent smaller outbuildings. To the left, there is an orchard area, where evenly spaced green trees dot a grassy area, some smaller shrubs line along one edge of the orchard. The largest section occupies the bottom and center of the drawing, consisting of an open green field sparsely planted with individual trees; a square gray feature (possibly a fountain or statue) is located near the bottom left corner of this field, with a nearby cluster of trees. The entire arrangement is enclosed by boundary fence lines, with additional rows of trees marking some edges. A brown road runs along the left and lower boundary, crossing a blue-gray stream at the bottom left. The background outside the main area is a light brown color, representing earth or fields, and there are a few groups of trees depicted beyond the main enclosed area. At the top, there is a small brownish-gray building located outside the main garden sections.
title: Eliza Jumel Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
